documents.title: Leave forms
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi! Quick admin question. I'm putting in for maternity leave starting in June and our leave vendor needs a provider certification. Do those come from you or from OB? (I work in HR so I should know this, but it's different when it's your own, ha.)

documents.title: RE: Leave forms
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Hi Yvette, for pregnancy-related leave the certification usually comes from the OB office since they are managing the pregnancy and will know the delivery date. If they ask for anything from primary care, send it over and we'll take care of it.

documents.title: OB visit: elevated blood pressure
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Re: Yvette Reed, DOB 02/01/1996. G2P1, 26w5d by early ultrasound.

Dear Doctor,

I saw Ms. Reed on 3/23/2026 to follow up a raised blood pressure from her last routine prenatal visit. Until that visit the pregnancy had been going smoothly. She has noticed headaches now and then and some puffiness of her hands and feet. No vision problems, no abdominal pain, no trouble breathing.

Blood pressure today 152/98 mmHg. Urine dipstick 2+ protein. CBC and metabolic panel drawn today were normal, including platelets 224, creatinine 0.58, AST 18 and ALT 15.

Ultrasound: fetal growth appropriate for dates, normal fluid, active fetus. Uterine artery Doppler shows a high-resistance pattern with reduced flow in diastole.

Assessment: preeclampsia without severe features at 26 weeks, in a patient with gestational hypertension in her first pregnancy, on aspirin 81 mg since 12 weeks.

Plan: expectant management. Blood pressure checks and fetal testing twice a week, preeclampsia labs weekly. If she remains without severe features, delivery is planned at 37 weeks. We reviewed warning signs (severe or persistent headache, visual changes, upper abdominal pain, shortness of breath) and she knows to go straight to the hospital for any of them. Continue prenatal vitamin, aspirin 81 mg nightly and calcium carbonate 500 mg twice daily. No antihypertensive at this time.

Allergies: NKDA.

Obstetrics & Gynecology

documents.title: Checking in
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Yvette, I got the note from your OB about the blood pressure and the preeclampsia diagnosis. I'm sorry, I know that's a lot to take in at 26 weeks. It sounds like they have a careful plan with twice-weekly checks. Please don't hesitate to go in for a bad headache or vision change; that's exactly what they want to hear about. Anything you need from us, just message.

documents.title: RE: Checking in
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thank you, that means a lot. Honestly I kind of expected it after last time and with my mom. I have my appointments lined up and I got a BP cuff. I'll keep you posted.

documents.title: Physical on 4/14

documents.body: Hi, I need to cancel my physical next Tuesday. Between OB twice a week and work I just can't fit another appointment in. Can we do it after the baby comes? Probably later in the summer or fall.

documents.title: RE: Physical on 4/14

documents.body: No problem, we cancelled 4/14. We'll put a reminder on your chart to schedule after delivery. Take care!

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PHYSICIAN RECORD
Date of service: 04/26/2026

CC: headache x3 days, 31 weeks pregnant

HPI: 30 yo G2P1 at 31w4d with preeclampsia without severe features diagnosed by OB about a month ago (gestational HTN in first pregnancy). Dull headache for 3 days that has not gone away with rest or an over-the-counter pain reliever. On and off discomfort in the upper abdomen. Legs and fingers somewhat swollen. Denies visual symptoms, SOB, fever, contractions. Baby moving normally. Sees OB twice weekly, no other problems this pregnancy.

Meds: prenatal vitamin, ASA 81 mg, calcium carbonate 500 mg BID. Allergies: NKDA.
PMH/PSH: obesity; C-section 2024; lap appy 2014.
SH: never smoker, no EtOH in pregnancy. HR coordinator.

Exam: BP 150/98 on arrival, 150/98 again on repeat. Alert, no distress. Neuro nonfocal. Heart regular, lungs clear. Abdomen gravid, soft, nontender, no RUQ tenderness. 1+ pitting edema both feet/ankles.

UA: protein 2+.
CBC, CMP: Hgb 11.5, plt 198, Cr 0.66, AST 22, ALT 19. No thrombocytopenia, renal or hepatic involvement.
OB bedside US: growth appropriate, normal AFV.
NST: reactive.

MDM: preeclampsia with worsening symptoms. Pressures are elevated but below the severe range on repeat, and labs show no severe features. Discussed with the on-call obstetrician, who evaluated her in the department and agrees with continued outpatient management.

Impression: preeclampsia without severe features, 31 weeks.
Disposition: discharged home with OB follow-up within 48 hours. Strict return precautions given for worse headache, vision changes, RUQ/epigastric pain, SOB, decreased fetal movement, bleeding or contractions.

Emergency Medicine

documents.title: RN call after ED visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: ED record received 4/27, reviewed with PCP. Called pt to check in. She is seeing OB this afternoon as planned, already scheduled from the ED. States she is taking it easy at home today. Reviewed when to go back in (bad headache, vision change, pain under the ribs, SOB). She has our number and OB triage number. No needs from us right now.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PHYSICIAN RECORD
Date of service: 05/13/2026

CC: severe headache, blurry vision, 34 weeks

HPI: 30 yo G2P1 at 34w0d, known preeclampsia without severe features under OB surveillance, gestational HTN in her first pregnancy. Two hours of severe headache with blurred vision. Seen here 4/26 for headache and discharged.

Meds: prenatal vitamin, aspirin 81 mg daily, calcium carbonate 500 mg BID. Allergies: NKDA.
PSH: low transverse C-section 2024, laparoscopic appendectomy.

Triage: BP 168/112, HR 88, RR 18, afebrile.
Exam: uncomfortable from headache, oriented. Fundi: no papilledema. Reflexes 3+ at knees and biceps. 2+ edema of both lower legs. Lungs clear. Gravid abdomen, soft.

Labs: Hgb 11.2, platelets 95,000, creatinine 1.2, AST 70, ALT 65, total bilirubin 0.5, LDH 248. UA 2+ protein. Smear reviewed by lab: no schistocytes.
Fetal monitoring: reactive tracing.

Assessment: preeclampsia with severe features (severe-range BP, cerebral/visual symptoms, platelets under 100k, creatinine 1.2, transaminases about double normal). Criteria for HELLP not met (LDH normal, no hemolysis on smear).

ED course: labetalol 20 mg IV given; magnesium sulfate bolus started per obstetric protocol. OB at bedside. Admitted to Labor & Delivery for delivery.

Emergency Medicine

documents.title: Operative report: repeat cesarean delivery
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OPERATIVE REPORT
Date of surgery: 05/13/2026

Preoperative diagnosis: intrauterine pregnancy at 34w0d; preeclampsia with severe features; prior low transverse cesarean.
Postoperative diagnosis: same; delivered.
Procedure: repeat low transverse cesarean delivery.
Anesthesia: spinal (platelets 95,000, cleared by anesthesia).
Findings: liveborn infant, handed to the waiting pediatric team. Normal-appearing uterus, tubes and ovaries.
EBL: within expected range for cesarean. No transfusion.
Complications: none.
Magnesium sulfate infusion continued throughout and for 24 hours postpartum.
Counts correct x2. Patient to recovery in stable condition.

Obstetrics & Gynecology

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted: 05/13/2026   Discharged: 05/17/2026

Admission diagnosis: preeclampsia with severe features at 34 weeks, without HELLP syndrome.
Discharge diagnoses: same, delivered; status post repeat low transverse cesarean.

Hospital course: Presented to the ED with severe headache and blurred vision; BP 168/112 with thrombocytopenia (95k), creatinine 1.2 and transaminases around 70. LDH and bilirubin normal, no schistocytes. Given IV labetalol with BP down to 148/96, started on magnesium sulfate for seizure prophylaxis, and delivered the same day by repeat low transverse cesarean under spinal anesthesia. Liveborn infant, cared for by the pediatric service. Magnesium stopped 24 hours after delivery. No seizure activity. Headache and vision cleared after delivery.

BP remained in the 140s-150s systolic on POD1, so nifedipine ER 30 mg daily was started 5/14 with good effect. POD2 labs improving: Hgb 10.1, platelets 121, creatinine 0.92, AST 46, ALT 54.

Incision clean, dry, intact. Tolerating diet, ambulating, voiding. Discharge BP 138/90.

Immunizations this pregnancy: Tdap 3/30/2026 (OB office); influenza and COVID-19 10/2025 (PCP).

Discharge medications:
- Nifedipine ER 30 mg PO daily (new)
- Ibuprofen 600 mg PO q6h prn pain (new)
- Prenatal vitamin daily (continue)
STOPPED: aspirin 81 mg, calcium carbonate.
Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up: home BP checks twice daily with log; PCP visit within 1 week for BP and repeat CBC/CMP; OB postpartum visit at 6 weeks. Return for BP 160/110 or higher, severe headache, visual change, chest pain, shortness of breath, heavy bleeding, or wound redness.

Obstetrics & Gynecology

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Hospital d/c summary received this morning (d/c 5/17 after repeat C/S for severe preeclampsia). Called pt for transitional care follow-up.
- Feeling sore but OK. No headache, no vision changes, no SOB or chest pain.
- Home BPs since discharge in the 130s-140s/80s-90s. Has taken nifedipine ER 30 mg this morning.
- Incision: no redness or drainage. Bleeding lighter.
- Meds reviewed: nifedipine ER 30 daily, ibuprofen 600 prn, prenatal vitamin. Aspirin and calcium stopped.
Reviewed reasons to call/go to the ED (BP 160/110 or higher, bad headache, vision change). Booked with PCP Thu 5/21 with labs.

documents.title: Hospital Follow-up / TCM
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
TCM visit, 8 days after delivery, 4 days after discharge. RN contact 5/18.

Summary of admission: at 34 weeks presented with severe headache and blurry vision, BP 168/112, platelets 95k, Cr 1.2, AST/ALT ~70/65; not HELLP. Mag + IV labetalol, repeat low transverse C-section 5/13 under spinal. Nifedipine ER 30 started 5/14. Discharged 5/17 at 138/90.

Today: feels much better. Headache gone since the day after delivery, vision normal. Incision a little sore, using ibuprofen once or twice a day. Bleeding light. Home readings mostly 130s/80s, a couple in the low 140s right after discharge. No chest pain, SOB, leg pain or swelling beyond mild ankle puffiness that is better. Sleeping in short stretches, has help from family. Mood OK, feels like herself. PHQ-9 3.

Meds: nifedipine ER 30 mg daily, ibuprofen 600 mg prn, prenatal vitamin.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: BP 136/86. Weight 90.2 kg. Comfortable. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, appropriately tender near incision; Pfannenstiel incision clean, well approximated, no erythema or drainage. Trace ankle edema. Neuro nonfocal.

A/P
1. Severe preeclampsia, now postpartum. BP improved on nifedipine, not at goal for stopping yet. Continue nifedipine ER 30 daily, home BPs twice a day, send log in 2 weeks. Repeat CBC/CMP today to confirm platelets, kidney and liver are recovering.
2. Post-op: healing well. Ibuprofen as needed is fine with her BP at this level.
3. Mood: screen negative, normal early postpartum adjustment. Told her to reach out if mood dips or does not lift; OB will screen again at 6 weeks.
4. Long-term: preeclampsia, on top of her earlier gestational HTN and family history, raises lifetime risk for hypertension and heart disease. We will follow BP, lipids and A1c every year. Will discuss more at the next visit.

RTC 6-7 weeks (after OB postpartum visit).

documents.title: OB postpartum visit
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Re: Yvette Reed, DOB 02/01/1996

Dear Doctor,

Ms. Reed was seen 6/24/2026 for her six-week postpartum visit after a repeat low transverse cesarean at 34 weeks on 5/13 for preeclampsia with severe features.

She is recovering well. Blood pressure 126/80 on nifedipine ER 30 mg daily. Incision fully healed. Lochia resolved. Postpartum depression screening negative.

She is on nifedipine ER 30 mg daily and a prenatal vitamin. Allergies: NKDA.

We discussed that she should start low-dose aspirin early in any future pregnancy. Ongoing blood pressure management and the decision on tapering nifedipine we leave with you, along with longer-term cardiovascular follow-up given her history.

Thank you for sharing her care.

Obstetrics & Gynecology
